blocks.content: Verify tool/test equipment calibration status before use.

items.definition: Before use in a Part 145 shop, specialized test equipment must have a current calibration label showing it is within its calibration interval. Out-of-calibration equipment produces invalid results and non-compliant records.
items.analogy: Like verifying a thermometer against a known reference before using it in a critical process — if the tool is inaccurate, your measurements are meaningless.

blocks.question: Before using a pitot-static test set in a Part 145 shop, what must a technician verify?
choices: That the equipment has a current calibration label and is within its calibration interval
That the equipment has been used on the same aircraft type previously
That the equipment is specifically listed on the shop's capability list
That the software version meets the avionics manufacturer's minimum requirements
blocks.feedback: Part 145 requires test equipment to be calibrated and within interval before use. Out-of-calibration equipment produces invalid readings and may create non-compliant maintenance records. Capability list, prior use, and software version are not the primary verification.
